title: An area's waiting work gets done over time instead of being cut to make room, and its lessons stay short
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour), and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher where its notes say the same.

**What this is for.** Each area of the code has a note in two parts: Lessons, read before every change in the area, and Waiting, work known there but not scheduled. A note has a size cap so it stays short enough to read before every change. The three busiest notes are at or near the cap, and most of each is Waiting. A Waiting entry leaves when a change happens to settle it, when a ticket is filed for it, or when it is cut down to make room, so detail is being squeezed out of entries that are still true. A6 will send more finds into these notes. John: "Harbour should converge work, even if slowly, and resist spiralling out and generating more work (unless it's tidying up)." On the notes: "I'd be happy to address the notes issue potentially next."

**What we want.** Lessons stay short enough to read before every change. Waiting work is not squeezed or cut to make room. And waiting work gets done: over time an area's waiting list shrinks, as tidying.

**Done when** no note loses a still-true entry, or its detail, to fit; each note's Lessons stay within today's size limit; and the next changes in a busy area do some of its waiting work, so its list shrinks without entries being dropped or turned into tickets.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** Lessons alone keep today’s cap and Waiting stops being cut, while each change names the entry it settled under a check; first, the note sizing and settling rule is stated once for every writer, since scattered restatements keep squeezing.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

**Implemented and closed (12 Nov 2026).** The plan (revision 2, approved at plan review) was implemented as approved, with no deviations:

* [LinearViewer #2399](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2399>), merged as `b349c219b` and deployed.
* [simple-dispatcher #337](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/337>), merged as `a42456c6f`.

What landed:

* Both guards cap only `## Lessons`, at 6144 B. Waiting is uncapped, and each note's Waiting count is printed in CI.
* Both READMEs say a Waiting entry leaves only when it is settled, made untrue or filed, never to make room.
* `lib/periodicals.js` no longer tells readings to shorten notes.
* Every stage build's leftover step settles one fix-sized Waiting entry and names it on a `Retires:` line, which the proxy holds with a 422.

Close-out removed the settled "SD's notes guard has diverged" entry and merged LIN-4420's `main` into the branch (`parseNote` now comes from the shared leaf).

Session fit: fits one session.

plan-review due: yes

The full design, plan, revisions and review history are preserved in the task snapshots and in the comment trail (Design, Plan, Plan Review, Implementation, Review and Close-out comments).

## Still watched

* **Monitor:** the guard's CI diagnostic `area-notes waiting <slug>: N entries` on `main`.
* **Baselines at merge:** runs-and-dispatch 16, llm-and-prompts 14, front-end-pages 13, agent-api 11.
* **Checkpoint 26 Nov 2026 (John's ruling):** if busy lists are not shrinking, the Periodical inflow limit goes back to John.

**Rollback:** revert both merge commits. This is clean only while every note fits the whole-file 6144 B cap after the revert.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4414 @ 30a019289

**What's there today.** The guard `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (check 4, `NOTE_BYTE_CAP = 6144`) caps the *whole file*, so Lessons and Waiting compete for the same bytes. `llm-and-prompts.md` is at 6143 B (Lessons ~2.4 KB, Waiting ~3.7 KB), `runs-and-dispatch.md` 5980, `front-end-pages.md` 5937 (Waiting ~4.8 KB). The squeeze is already visible: entries like "(Area reads CG/CH.)" are compressed past the point a cold reader can follow them. simple-dispatcher's notes are all under 3 KB, so it only needs to keep the format in step, and its guard copy has already drifted.

**Why this will be hard.**

1. **The cap is a symptom. The real problem is inflow beating outflow.** 66 of the 83 Waiting entries come from Periodical readings, not from changes in the area. `periodicalBullet.areaNotes()` in `lib/periodicals.js` tells about ten templates to add entries. Outflow is weak by design: `lib/prompt-formatters.js` and `docs/areas/README.md` both say "Waiting entries are context, not scope". Uncapping Waiting alone lets the list grow without limit, which goes against John's "resist spiralling out".
2. **"Waiting gets done" needs a mechanism, and prompt words won't hold one.** The note's own Lesson says so (LIN-4369): hold the shape in code or a test. To be checkable, a retired entry has to appear in the size record (`lib/size-of-move.js`) or the leftover step (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js`). Many entries are larger tidies ("fold ~nine parallel tables into one definition") that won't settle in passing.
3. **Changing the wording is expensive here.** The prompt budget is frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`), scoping and Survey renders are kept byte-identical for replays, and `docs/areas/` is spelled in 17 lines across 10 code files. `LEFTOVER_RULE` and "context, not scope" are each rendered verbatim in several stages, so every edit means re-measuring ceilings and snapshots.
4. **Retiring "context, not scope" is arguably John's call.** It was put there on purpose against scope creep. John's "unless it's tidying up" leans towards retiring it, but it should go to him as a ruling.

**What I'd do first.** Split the cap. Keep the 6144-byte cap on `## Lessons` only, measured per section in `checkAreaNotes`, and give Waiting a separate, generous cap or its own file that only scoping reads. That stops the loss with a one-test change, plus the README and the simple-dispatcher mirror. Then deal with outflow as a separate move: a checkable "retires: `<entry>`" line in the size record or leftovers whenever an area has fix-sized entries, a per-note count so shrinkage can be measured, and Periodicals pruning before they add. Until then, remove or ticket no entry just to make room.

## Survey global: LIN-4414 @ 30a019289

**Where it lands.** `docs/areas/` (11 notes, README), the guard `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (check 4: whole file ≤ 6144 B), and the writers: `periodicalBullet.areaNotes()` in `lib/periodicals.js` (16 call sites), the leftover step in `lib/dispatch-leftover.js`, `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`, and `formatAreaNotesPointer()` in `lib/prompt-formatters.js`. simple-dispatcher has its own copy of the guard (`test/area-notes.test.js`, same cap, drifted). Its notes are all under 3 KB.

**What it's like now.** Tidy in form, and the guard is mutation-tested. But it fills faster than it empties. Harbour's Waiting entries went from 30 to 83 between 8 and 11 Nov. Lessons are small: 2.7 KB at most (`runs-and-dispatch`), and three notes have none. Waiting is 55–80% of each busy note. `llm-and-prompts.md` is at 6143 B. The squeeze is written in code: `areaNotes()` tells each reading to "prune entries… and distil it so it stays under its cap". About half the entries cite a Periodical report. Several writers add entries; nothing removes them except by accident (a change happens to settle one, or a follow-up is filed). Builders are told "Waiting entries are context, not scope". So the cap is the symptom. Underneath, the flow is one-way, and it is getting worse.

**Done the obvious way** (cap Lessons, uncap Waiting): this ends the squeeze but removes the only brake. Waiting grows without limit, and "read before every change" turns into reading a backlog. A separate Waiting file would add a second home and break guard check 1. README, both cap phrases in `periodicals.js`, the pointer, and SD's guard and README would all need to learn about it. Only the guard tests would notice if they didn't; the prompt restatements drift silently, which an existing Waiting entry already records. The outflow half collides with "context, not scope", a deliberate anti-creep rule. Bending it is John's call. Outflow added only as prompt words would break the area's LIN-4369 Lesson: hold it in code or a test.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Check 4 measures `## Lessons` against 6144 B. Waiting stays uncapped, with a per-note count printed so shrinkage is visible.
- `areaNotes()` stops telling readings to distil Waiting and points to README instead of restating its rules. That settles a `llm-and-prompts` Waiting entry: waiting work done.
- The leftover answer names a Waiting entry it settled in its area, or says why none fit, and a shape check enforces it the way `checkSizeRecord` does. That is "names what it retires".
- SD parity in the same move.
- Change the guard before adding any Lesson to `llm-and-prompts` (1 byte of room).

**Better still, not this task's:** one shared guard for both repos; Periodicals deduplicating against existing entries before adding; a ceiling on Periodical inflow (what to stop reading is John's call); folding the parallel per-kind tables in `prompt-template-defs.js`, where much of `llm-and-prompts` Waiting points.

## Design: LIN-4414 @ 30a019289

**Re-grounding.** The surveys measured `30a019289`, which is still HEAD of LinearViewer `main`. Since the ticket was filed (21:42 on 11 Nov), the files it cites changed only in docs: LIN-4418 and LIN-4413 readings added Waiting entries, and LIN-4415 added an `llm-and-prompts` Lesson. Today, at HEAD: `llm-and-prompts.md` is 6143 B (Lessons 2350 B, 15 Waiting entries), `runs-and-dispatch.md` is 5980 B (Lessons 2688 B, 16 entries), `front-end-pages.md` is 5937 B (Lessons 1013 B, 13 entries) and `agent-api.md` is 5549 B (Lessons 1461 B, 11 entries). Across Harbour, Waiting went from 0 to 56 when the notes were seeded on 8–9 Nov, then to 75 on 11 Nov and 83 on 12 Nov. The largest Lessons section is 2688 B, well under 6144. Simple-dispatcher's notes are all under 3 KB. Its guard (`test/area-notes.test.js`) has the same whole-file check 4.

### The problem, from the cause

Three causes, and only the first is about the cap:

1. **Lessons and Waiting share one byte budget.** Check 4 in `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` caps the whole file at 6144 B. Waiting is 55–80 % of each busy note, so every new entry pushes against the cap and Lessons get no room of their own. You can see the squeeze in the history: "within the note's cap" (`23f9d58fc`), "runs-and-dispatch headroom" (`94c9d2e39`), and entries cut down to "(Area reads CG/CH.)".
2. **The squeeze is written into a writer.** `periodicalBullet.areaNotes()` (`lib/periodicals.js`) tells all 16 Periodical templates to "distil it so it stays under its cap". The bound line in the same file adds "each note under its cap". So the readings that add most entries are also told to shorten the ones already there.
3. **Entries flow in but only leave by accident.** About two thirds of the entries come from Periodical readings. An entry leaves only when a change happens to settle it, when a follow-up is filed for it, or when it is cut to fit. Builders are told "Waiting entries are context, not scope" (`formatAreaNotesPointer()`, `docs/areas/README.md`), so nothing makes a change do waiting work.

A good outcome has four parts. Lessons stay within today's 6144 B. No true entry is cut or shortened to make room. Each change in a busy area settles some of that area's waiting work and names what it settled. The guard's counts show whether each busy list is shrinking.

### Shapes considered

**A. Cap Lessons only, and stop telling writers to fit.** Check 4 measures the `## Lessons` section against 6144 B. Waiting has no cap. `areaNotes()` loses its distil sentence and points to the README for the rules.
- *Cost:* small. About 20 lines of guard, two prompt clauses, README edits, the same in simple-dispatcher.
- *Fit:* reuses the existing guard and note format, with one home.
- *Risk:* it ends the squeeze but takes away the only brake. With nothing taking entries out, Waiting grows without limit. That goes against "resist spiralling out" and does not meet "its list shrinks". **Necessary, not sufficient.**

**B. A on its own file: Waiting moves to `docs/areas/<slug>.waiting.md`.** Only scoping reads that file.
- *Cost:* medium. It is a second home for each area. It breaks guard check 1 (one file per slug) and needs changes to the README, both pointers, every writer, and simple-dispatcher's guard.
- *Risk:* the scattered prompt restatements of the note rules drift without anyone noticing, which an existing Waiting entry already records (`lib/periodicals.js`, Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov). Moving entries out of sight also does nothing to get them done. **Rejected.** It adds a second way of doing the same thing and leaves the cause untouched.

**C. A, plus a checked retirement at the leftover step (recommended).**
- A note is **busy** when its Waiting holds **8 or more entries**. Today that is `runs-and-dispatch` (16), `llm-and-prompts` (15), `front-end-pages` (13) and `agent-api` (11). The other seven notes have 2–6 entries.
- When a stage build's leftover step runs (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js`, once per ticket, in the builder's own session), and the change touched a busy area, the builder settles **one fix-sized Waiting entry** of that area on the PR branch and removes it in the same change.
- The `### Leftovers` answer carries one **`Retires:`** line in a fixed shape. It either quotes the entry it settled (its cited path and opening words), or it says `none` with a reason from a closed list:
  - *not busy*: no area the change touched has a busy note;
  - *nothing fix-sized*: the line names the smallest entry and says why it is larger.
- Code holds the shape the way `checkSizeRecord` holds the size record (LIN-4369 arm 3). The proxy refuses a comment that opens `### Leftovers` without a valid `Retires:` line, with 422 and a code. Review already reads "the diff against the builder's `### Leftovers` comment" (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`). A retirement the diff does not show is caught there, so review needs no new words.
- Larger entries keep the path they already have. Scoping weighs note entries, the standing policy is "err larger", and a move that takes an entry on settles it.
- *Cost:* medium. One small pure checker module (`lib/dispatch-leftover-answer.js`, maps to `runs-and-dispatch`, reads its spelling from the `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` leaf), one guard call in `routes/proxy-writes.js` createComment, about 250 B more in the leftover prompt (a ceiling raise with its reason), A's guard and README work, and simple-dispatcher parity. Each build in a busy area also costs a little more, because the builder does one small fix and review reads it.
- *Fit:* reuses everything. The leftover step already resumes the builder to tidy the change's edges. `LEFTOVER_RULE` and the `### Leftovers` heading already have one home. The proxy already holds description shapes the same way. Scoping, the Survey renders and the stage pointer do not change, so the byte-identical replay constraint is untouched.
- *Risks:*
  - a builder could claim it settled an entry it did not (review's diff read catches this);
  - a leftover answer posted outside the proxy lane goes unchecked (the size record has the same limit, and it is accepted there);
  - a busy note whose entries are all larger shrinks only through scoping.

**D. A, plus a scheduled tidy run.** A new corrective Periodical takes the busiest note and settles several fix-sized entries in one PR.
- *Cost:* medium. A new template, a schedule (Periodicals are opt-in since LIN-4415), and its own prompt surface.
- *Risk:* each run is a ticket made from waiting entries, which is close to the "turned into tickets" the ask rules out. It also works beside changes in the area rather than through them, while the ask says "the next changes in a busy area do some of its waiting work". **I keep it in reserve** in case C's outflow cannot keep up (see below).

### Recommendation: C

C is the only shape that stops the loss (A's half) and also makes waiting work leave through actual work, recorded in a checked line. It does this inside the area's LIN-4369 Lesson: the shape is held in code, not in prompt words. It also settles existing Waiting entries as part of the move.

**What this change itself retires:**
- check 4's whole-file cap;
- the "distil it so it stays under its cap" sentence and the "each note under its cap" clause in `lib/periodicals.js`;
- the `llm-and-prompts` Waiting entry `lib/periodicals.js`: "`areaNotes()` restates the notes' own rules" (Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov). `areaNotes()` points to the README instead;
- the `llm-and-prompts` Waiting entry `lib/periodicals.js`: "SD's notes guard has diverged …" (Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov), in full or not at all. Both guards are brought to the same functions, and SD's README gains the Periodical-entry rules. The plan decides whether SD's existence check can accept a citation to a LinearViewer report. If it cannot, that entry stays and the change says so.

**Key implementation points (for the plan):**
- **Guard** (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, and SD's copy):
  - check 4 measures the bytes from `## Lessons` to the next `##` against `NOTE_BYTE_CAP` (6144), with an exported `BUSY_WAITING_ENTRIES` (8);
  - a diagnostic prints each note's Waiting count and busy flag;
  - the guard asserts that the README states both numbers, so the README restatement cannot drift;
  - mutation tests: a large Lessons section fails check 4, a large Waiting section passes, and a README without the numbers fails.
- **README** (both repos):
  - "The guard" says Lessons are capped and Waiting is not;
  - an entry leaves only when it is settled, made untrue, or filed, and never to make room;
  - "One home" gains the busy rule and the `Retires:` line;
  - "context, not scope" stays for the build itself, and the leftover step's one retirement in a busy area is the exception.
- **`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`:** add the `Retires:` label and the closed list of `none` reasons. It stays a leaf.
- **`lib/dispatch-leftover.js` `leftoverPrompt`:** one sentence. In a busy area (its README says when), settle one fix-sized waiting entry and name it on a `Retires:` line, or say `none` and why.
- **`routes/proxy-writes.js`:** a `refusedByLeftoverAnswer` check in createComment and updateComment, active only when the body has the `### Leftovers` heading line. Every other comment is untouched.
- **Prompt budget:** raise `LEFTOVER_PROMPT_RENDERED_CEILING` with the LIN-4414 reason. The Periodical render shrinks, so update its sha256 tripwire and change-log row. Re-measure after a rebase, because `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge.
- **Change order:** change the guard before any Lesson lands in `llm-and-prompts.md`, which has 1 B of room today.

**What would change my mind:**
- **The counts don't fall.** If the guard's counts show the busy notes not shrinking after about two weeks of builds in them, Periodical inflow is outrunning C's outflow. The next move would be D, or a limit on Periodical inflow into busy notes. What to stop reading is John's call, so I have left it out.
- **The answer is usually "nothing fix-sized".** If leftover answers in one busy note mostly say that, the note's entries are bigger than a passing fix. Scoping's size of move would then need teeth there.
- **Waiting gets too long to read.** If a busy note's Waiting grows past about twice the Lessons cap, so that reading it before every change costs something real, I would weigh B's separate scoping-only file despite its second home.

### Area notes weighed
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Lesson: "Prompt words banning a kind of how do not hold it … Hold the shape in code or a test" (LIN-4369). This is why the `Retires:` shape gets a proxy check.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Lesson: prompt size is frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`). This is why the leftover ceiling is raised with its reason.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Lesson: shared words go in an import-free leaf (LIN-4376). The new spelling goes in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Lesson: keep scoping and both Survey renders byte-identical (LIN-4369). C leaves the pointer and scoping untouched.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Lesson: `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge (LIN-4393). Rebase, then re-measure.
- `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, Lesson: "The store knows no leftovers" (LIN-4383). The check goes in the proxy and a pure module, never in `lib/dispatch-store.js`.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Waiting: the two `lib/periodicals.js` entries above, which this move settles.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, Waiting: the Periodical-prompt ceiling entry (Documentation Review, 10 Nov). This is context only and not taken on.

### Cuts and rulings

DECISION: **Cuts: none.** Each clause of `## As asked` is delivered as follows:
- "Lessons stay short enough to read before every change" and "each note's Lessons stay within today's size limit": check 4 measures Lessons against 6144 B.
- "Waiting work is not squeezed or cut to make room" and "no note loses a still-true entry, or its detail, to fit": Waiting is uncapped and the distil instruction is gone.
- "the next changes in a busy area do some of its waiting work, so its list shrinks without entries being dropped or turned into tickets": the leftover step's checked retirement, which counts settled entries only, never filed ones, with counts the guard prints.
- "simple-dispatcher where its notes say the same": SD parity.
- "Every change names what it retires": the `Retires:` line, and this change's own list above.

I read the ask's "the next changes in a busy area do some of its waiting work … as tidying" as John's own ruling on the "context, not scope" rule that both surveys flagged. C bends that rule only in busy areas and only at the leftover step. The build itself still treats Waiting as context.

One question for John, which does not block planning. **Should Periodical inflow into busy notes stay unlimited for now?** I recommend yes. Measure for two weeks with the guard's counts, and only if busy lists are not falling, rule on limiting what Periodicals add (what to stop reading is your call).

## Plan written: LIN-4414 @ 30a019289

The implementation plan is now in the description, under `## Implementation Plan`. **Cuts: none.** It fits one session, as two PRs (LinearViewer, then simple-dispatcher, which is independent). Plan review is due.

**Two departures from the Design, both engineering calls:**

- **D1. No busy threshold.** Every stage build settles one fix-sized Waiting entry, in the touched area with the most entries, or says `none` with a reason from a closed list. With a threshold of 8, every list under 8 would have no outflow at all. That would quietly cut "over time an area's waiting list shrinks".
- **The `areaNotes()` drift entry is retired only in part.** The restatement half is settled. Its second clause (`docs/areas/` spelled in 17 lines across 10 code files) is still true, so it stays.

**Resolved open question:** simple-dispatcher's existence check needs no change. Its README already names Harbour paths in prose, and the two Periodical entries in its notes already cite LinearViewer reports that way. Its README gains the Periodical-entry rules that say so, which lets the guard-divergence entry retire in full.

**Still open to John (does not block):** whether Periodical inflow stays unlimited while the counts are measured.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes. The design is right, but the proxy check's trigger (D3) would also refuse review verdicts, because reviewers already post a `### Leftovers` heading line of their own.

Blocking findings: 1

**How the plan meets what was asked:**
- "each note's Lessons stay within today's size limit": check 4 measures `## Lessons` only, against 6144 B.
- "no note loses a still-true entry, or its detail, to fit": Waiting has no cap, both squeeze clauses in `lib/periodicals.js` go, and the README says an entry never leaves to make room.
- "the next changes in a busy area do some of its waiting work, so its list shrinks without entries being dropped or turned into tickets": every stage build makes one checked retirement at the leftover step, and a filed ticket never counts. The plan does not narrow the ask.
- D1 widens "a busy area" to every touched area. That is not a narrowing, and it falls inside "over time an area's waiting list shrinks". The block's own words ask changes to do waiting work as tidying, so bending "context, not scope" at the leftover step needs no separate ruling.

**What I checked.** Both HEADs are unchanged since grounding: LinearViewer `30a019289` and simple-dispatcher `7d6c5c6`. Since the ticket was filed, only `docs/areas/` changed. I read these at HEAD:
- `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, where check 4 measures the whole file;
- `lib/periodicals.js:314` and `:347`, which hold both squeeze clauses;
- `lib/dispatch-leftover.js` `leftoverPrompt` and `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`;
- `routes/proxy-writes.js`, the comment POST and PATCH handlers (the dedupe cache is only set on success, so a refused body is never cached in any case);
- `refusedBySizeRecord` as the model for the new check, and the `SIZE_RECORD_CODES` import in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`;
- both READMEs, simple-dispatcher's guard (it already has `sh`), and the budget constants.

The premises hold:
- `llm-and-prompts.md` is 6143 B.
- The LinearViewer README already states the Periodical citation format, so `areaNotes()` can safely delegate to it.
- 13 corrective templates render `areaNotes()`, and the 3 advisory templates do not.
- LIN-4415's own leftover answer says it "shortened [a lesson] ... to fit the note's 6,144-byte cap". That is the squeeze, seen live.

#### Blocking

**1. D3's trigger catches review verdicts, not just the builder's answer.** D3 acts on "a comment that has a line which, trimmed, is exactly the `LEFTOVERS_HEADING`". The plan's "How I know every place is found" says "Nothing else posts that heading". That search covered code only. The heading is also written by agents in prose, because review's template sends them to "the builder's `### Leftovers` comment". I sampled six recent tickets:
- The reviews on **LIN-4378** (08 Nov 10:50) and **LIN-4393** (08 Nov 15:32) each have a standalone `### Leftovers` line, as a subsection of `## Review — …`.
- Every builder answer in the sample (LIN-4415, 4378, 4369, 4393, 4376) **starts with** `### Leftovers` as its first line.

Built as written, the check would refuse these review verdicts with 422. A reviewer would then either fail to post the verdict that gates merge, or follow the refusal message and add a `Retires:` line. That second outcome puts false retirement claims into review comments and corrupts the signal W8 measures. No witness in the plan would catch this, because W3 and W4 use builder answers only.

*Change:*
- Describe the behaviour as "the builder's leftover answer: a comment whose **first non-blank line**, trimmed, is `LEFTOVERS_HEADING`". This is what the Design said ("a comment that opens `### Leftovers`").
- Change the leftover prompt's "post your answer … under `### Leftovers`" so it asks for a comment that *starts with* the heading. The extra bytes are part of the measured ceiling raise.
- Add to W3: the real LIN-4393 review comment, which contains a `### Leftovers` subsection, passes untouched.
- Add to W4: a review-shaped POST with a mid-comment heading line returns 201.
- Fix the sentence in "every place is found" to name agent prose (review verdicts) as a second writer of the heading line.

#### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

- **W1 mutation shape.** The 7 KB Waiting growth has to be made of valid entries, meaning bullets whose first cited path maps to the note's area. Otherwise check 3 fires. Assert `checksOf(...)` is `[]`, not just "no check 4".
- **README guard text.** Item 4 now says "settle or drop stale entries". When you rewrite it under D7, say "settled or no longer true", and drop any wording that reads as removing entries for space.
- **Count correction.** `areaNotes()` has 13 call sites (`lib/periodicals.js` lines 415 to 967), not 16. Sixteen is the number of Periodical renders. The witnesses are unaffected.
- **Second unchecked copy of the answer.** The leftover prompt also asks the builder to end the session with the same answer, as its terminal message, and the check does not see that copy. That is fine, because review reads the comment, but say so beside the D4 residual in `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`.
- **Refusal message.** Give the three forms with one literal example each, as `recordShape()` does. Then a builder refused once can fix it in a single retry.
- **This build's own retirement.** Under D1, this build's new module lives in `runs-and-dispatch`, which has 16 entries, so its own leftover step should name an entry there if the new prompt is deployed by then. If it is not deployed, say so in the answer.
